trajectory.thought: The leader is a seeded baseline (median of full pool) and the verdict is "indistinguishable" — the runner-up is not statistically better. The series has unstable model ranking (Kendall tau 0.259), very high error correlation (0.898), and only 3 validation windows, all of which favor a robust, simple combination over fitted weights. The median already captures the robustness the diagnosis calls for, and with 19 highly correlated models, pruning or re-weighting is unlikely to produce a real gain over 3 noisy windows.

action_args.justification: The series is stationary with moderate trend and seasonality, medium predictability, and a noisy regime. Model ranking is unstable (Kendall tau 0.259) and error correlation is very high (mean 0.898, only 2 independent groups), so most of the 19 models carry redundant information. Under these conditions a robust median of the full pool is the natural choice: it is insensitive to the few outlying models, does not chase window-specific ranking noise, and avoids the high-variance weight estimation that only 3 validation windows would permit. The leader's margin over the runner-up is not statistically distinguishable, confirming that no simpler or more complex combination offers a reliable improvement.
